phases.name: Constitution
phases.does: Apply scripted amendments due today. If a proposal is pending from yesterday, every chamber member casts an amendment ballot, then a referendum may follow.

phases.name: Snapshot
phases.does: Write one row per citizen to snapshots.jsonl, before anything moves.

phases.name: Rupture candidacies
phases.does: A small random draw lets a citizen far from their party stand as a protest candidate.

phases.name: Exogenous events
phases.does: Draw a scandal against the president, and step the AR(1) economy; a shock when |x| crosses the threshold.

phases.name: Presidential election
phases.does: Resolve a refusal to leave first; then candidacy, party nomination, campaign, ballots, count, term.

phases.name: Legislative election
phases.does: Party-list vote (sincere, then one strategic round), seats by D'Hondt, then coalition formation.

phases.name: Sortition chamber
phases.cadence: rotation every 4 ticks; deliberation every tick (LLM only)
phases.does: Reseat the chamber by lot; members deliberate and may shift their chamber position.

phases.name: Leaders
phases.cadence: every tick, with the president agent
phases.does: The president's turn: restate positions, draft a bill, propose an amendment, or act extra-legally.

phases.name: Forum
phases.cadence: every tick, with the forum agents
phases.does: Recent petition launchers and chamber members post; a post can change a mind or move a party membership.

phases.name: Legislation
phases.cadence: a bill every 2 ticks; a suspended bill's second reading when due
phases.does: Draft, then assembly vote, cohabitation block, chamber review, enactment.

phases.name: Emotions
phases.does: Appraise anger, anxiety and enthusiasm against the president and the economy; update engagement.

phases.name: Accountability
phases.cadence: every tick, when mandate, legitimacy or awakening is on
phases.does: The citizens' side of the loop (_run_accountability_phase), in this order:
sub: Reaction to today's events, the whole population, scandal first
Awakening gate, then one pressure action per consulted citizen; petitions launched and signed
Petition reaches its threshold (confidence vote) or expires
Below the legitimacy floor: a confidence vote (ADR-025)

phases.name: Snap election
phases.cadence: when the office is vacant and nothing is scheduled
phases.does: Schedule a rerun for next tick (with snap_election_on_recall).

phases.name: Opinion dynamics
phases.cadence: every tick, when enabled; deliberately last
phases.does: Friedkin-Johnsen: citizens move toward neighbours within the confidence bound, pulled back to their anchor.

calendar.name: Calendar & terms
calendar.when: Pure arithmetic on the tick, consulted by every election phase.
calendar.inputs: The tick; the holder's mandates served and short terms.
calendar.decision: Presidential election when tick % 16 == 0; legislative when (tick − 8) % 16 == 0. A winner's term ends at the next calendar election, so a snap winner only serves the rest of the term. A term won with less than half of it left is a short term and does not count toward the limit: counted = mandates − short_terms, term-limited when counted ≥ limit (also the lame-duck flag).

rupture.name: Rupture candidacy
rupture.when: Every tick, before events and elections.
rupture.who: Every elector (a random number is drawn for each, even the gated ones, to keep the stream stable).
rupture.inputs: Distance to the citizen's own party platform; the share of others who find them acceptable.
rupture.decision: p = 0.001 × (1 + 2.0 × d); draw u < p, then require ballot access: at least 0.5% of other citizens within their own tolerance of this one. Term-limited and barred citizens are skipped after the draw. Never asks the LLM.

candidacy.name: Candidacy & nomination
candidacy.when: On a presidential election tick (or 4 and 1 ticks before, with a staggered election).
candidacy.who: On the LLM engine, the whole population is asked whether to run; then each party with two or more declared members chooses its nominee.
candidacy.inputs: Candidacy: ambition and perceived support (the share of citizens who find you acceptable), TOON-encoded. Nomination: each declared member's position, ambition, support, distance to the platform.
candidacy.decision: Candidacy (candidacy_considered, batches of 25, no thinking): outcome 0/1 and a motif (201, 203, 204, 205). Rule: ambition ≥ 0.30. Nomination (party_nomination_choice, no thinking): winner_position 1..N and a motif (206–209); parties with 0 or 1 declared use the highest-ambition tiebreak. Term-limited and barred citizens are filtered after the answer. Independents are never nominated.
candidacy.schema: CandidacyDecision: cid, outcome, motif · PartyNominationDecision: party_id, winner_position, motif
candidacy.fallback: Per chunk: the ambition threshold. Nomination: whole batch, then each party alone, then the highest-ambition member.

campaign.name: Campaign: positioning & salience
campaign.inputs: A vote-intention poll (first choices, blank and abstain shares), the field, the nominee's platform against the public median.
campaign.decision: Without agents, campaign_positioning (one batch, thinking): up to 3 shifts of ≤ 0.3. With agents.nominees, a nominee_turn per nominee: position targets, plus a campaign plan (an issue and an audience: the party base, or the undecided). Reached citizens (capped at max_reached) get that issue's priority raised: p += step·(1 − p), the others scaled down, so priorities still sum to 1.
campaign.schema: PositioningDecision: cid, shifts, motif · CampaigningNomineeTurn: rationale, positions, speech, campaign{issue, audience}
campaign.fallback: No shift, motif 601; a failed nominee turn keeps the platform where it was.

presidential.name: Presidential election
presidential.when: Presidential ticks, or a pending rerun or snap election.
presidential.who: Every engaged citizen votes; the field is the nominees plus standing rupture candidates.
presidential.inputs: Each candidate's pledged platform; the voter's positions, priorities and tolerance; optionally the incumbent's record.
presidential.decision: Counted ballots are utility ballots (vote.mode = utility): utility = −weighted distance + partisanship + approval × record (2L − 1) + policy retrospection + valence; candidates within tolerance rank above Blank. A voter abstains when their best candidate is worth about a blank (turnout_cost). The LLM casts vote_cast only on a 10% audit sample that is never counted, unless vote.mode = llm. Count: two-round by default (13 ranked methods available); Blank is an ordinary label and can win.
presidential.fallback: An LLM ballot falls back to the distance ranking (motif 101/105).

presidential.note: If more than half of ballots put Blank first and blank_vote_competitive is on, the election is invalidated and rerun next tick with the field barred; the third attempt is forced.

legislative.name: Legislative election
legislative.inputs: Party platforms; governing parties' policy record.
legislative.decision: Sincere vote for the nearest party (or blank beyond tolerance). Then one strategic round (ADR-024): the sincere vote is the poll; a voter whose party is under the 5% threshold moves to the best viable party if it costs ≤ strategic_margin. Seats by D'Hondt over 100 seats, threshold measured on the party vote. No LLM.

coalition.name: Coalition formation
coalition.who: The formateur (largest party) and every other seated party, or their leaders.
coalition.inputs: Seats, the majority threshold, the provisional total, what the others said last round.
coalition.decision: Rule: add seated parties in ascending distance from the formateur until seats exceed half. LLM: each party says join or leave (coalition_decision), up to 3 rounds, stopping at a fixed point. With agents.coalition each party's most ambitious member takes a coalition_turn (rationale, join yes/no, statement).
coalition.schema: CoalitionDecision: party_id, action (1 join, 2 leave), motif · LeaderCoalitionTurn: rationale, join, statement
coalition.fallback: None on the batch path: a failed round means coalition_failed and no government. A leader with no answer keeps their previous one, or declines in round 1.
coalition.note: Measured: the batch path tends to answer join whatever the content.

chamber.name: Sortition chamber
chamber.when: Rotation every 4 ticks; deliberation every tick on the LLM engine.
chamber.who: Citizens drawn uniformly by lot from those who never served and hold no office.
chamber.inputs: Deliberation sees only ticks_left: the chamber is insulated from every pressure channel.
chamber.decision: chamber_deliberation (chunks of 5, thinking): up to 3 shifts of ≤ 0.3 to the member's chamber position, motif 701 (no shift) or 702. Shifts accumulate over the term. The chamber reviews bills and votes on amendments.
chamber.fallback: Per chunk: motif 701, no shift. A 702 with no shift is relabelled 701.

president_turn.name: President's turn
president_turn.when: Every tick, with the president agent.
president_turn.inputs: A stable persona (party, top issues, ambition, views on all 20 issues) and goal; each tick: approval, legitimacy, street pressure, gap from the pledge, a per-issue table (policy, stated position, pledge, public and assembly medians), the constitution, the stakes, and memory (last 16 public events, own last 8 turns).
president_turn.decision: president_turn (thinking): restate positions (each step ≤ 0.3), draft a bill (if the agenda is open), propose an amendment, or declare refuse_to_leave. Free text is kept: speech, rationale, note to self.
president_turn.schema: LeaderTurn: rationale, positions, bill, speech, note_to_self, other_initiative (+ amendment, + extra_legal)
president_turn.fallback: Every attempt failed: no move, the formula drafts the bill, silence.

response.inputs: Legitimacy, mandate deviation, last tick's street pressure (a structural one-tick lag), lame-duck, ticks left.

events.name: Exogenous events & reactions
events.when: Events drawn every tick (phase 4); reactions at the start of accountability, scandal first.
events.who: The whole population, every citizen, no gate.
events.inputs: Each citizen's current event salience; the event type, target and magnitude.
events.decision: Scandal: Bernoulli(0.05) per tick against the president. Economy: x = 0.8·x + 0.1·ε, a shock when |x| ≥ 0.5. Reaction (reaction_to_event, batches of 25): a salience increase in [0, 0.3] and a motif (401, 402, or 403 = irrelevant, iff 0). Salience then decays: E = 0.85·E + delta.
events.fallback: A flat delta for everyone (scandal 0.3; shock 0.3 × min(1, |x|)).

engagement.name: Engagement & exit
engagement.decision: With hysteresis: anger ≥ exit level exits for good; ≥ disengage level disengages; a disengaged citizen returns once anger ≤ the return level. A disengaged or exited citizen does not vote, sign or join a confidence vote, but is still consulted, can still launch and mobilise, reacts, posts and can be drawn for the chamber.

awakening.name: Awakening gate
awakening.when: Accountability, for a seated president with a revealed position.
awakening.who: Decides which citizens are consulted at all.
awakening.inputs: Self gap (distance to the president's revealed position), base threshold, mandate deviation, election proximity, event salience, neighbours who mobilised last tick, emotion pull.
awakening.decision: threshold = base × f, with f = 1 − a·deviation + a·proximity − a·salience − a·neighbours − a·emotion clamped to [1 − a, 1 + a], a = 0.5 (each term only when its flag is on). Consulted iff self_gap > threshold. No cap, ordered by id; engagement is not checked.
events: (none: shows up as which pressure_action events exist)

pressure.name: Pressure action
pressure.when: Accountability step 2, right after the gate.
pressure.who: The consulted cohort, all of it, one citizen per call.
pressure.inputs: Frozen for the whole cohort before any act applies: self gap, mandate deviation, neighbours acting, ticks to election, the acts available to this citizen, the open petition, the tolerance signal, and emotions when enabled.
pressure.decision: pressure_action (no thinking, chunk of 1): an act (0 nothing, 1 sign, 2 launch a petition, 3 mobilise, 4 wait for the election) and a motif (301, 304, 305, 306). Acts are applied in id order against the live petition: a launch becomes a sign if a petition opened earlier in the loop. Mobilising adds to street pressure and to the neighbours' gate next tick.
pressure.fallback: Rule: nothing when the gap is under tolerance; otherwise sign, else launch, else mobilise, else wait.

pressure.note: The field order is decisive here: with motif written before act the model acted for 23 of 24 ground-truth citizens (EXP-025). Production sends cid, target, act, motif.

petitions.name: Petitions, confidence votes & recall
petitions.when: Accountability steps 3–6, per holder, after the pressure loop; the snap election in phase 13.
petitions.who: Signers; then every engaged citizen in a confidence vote.
petitions.inputs: Signature count against the population; each voter's tolerance of the president's revealed position.
petitions.decision: A petition collects for 4 ticks; at 25% of the population a confidence vote is held: each engaged citizen keeps the president iff their revealed position is within tolerance; retained iff keep > 50% (a tie removes), and a kept president's mandate becomes the keep ratio. Below the legitimacy floor, ADR-025 calls a confidence vote instead of recalling outright. A recall vacates the office; with snap elections on, a rerun is scheduled for next tick.

legitimacy.name: Legitimacy
legitimacy.inputs: Mandate strength m (share of ballots that ranked them above Blank), approval, petition pressure, street pressure.
legitimacy.decision: écart = 0.5·petition + 0.5·street (+ erosion·deviation); support blends m with approval; L = 0.9·L + 0.1·support − écart, clamped to [0, 1] (with pressure_like_support, écart is also damped by 0.1). Below the 0.2 floor: recall, or a confidence vote under ADR-025.

forum.name: Forum, minds & parties
forum.when: Every tick, with the forum agents.
forum.who: Recent petition launchers (last 8 ticks), then chamber members; at most 30, in parallel, blind to each other's same-tick posts.
forum.inputs: A persona; the party roll; whether a founding would reach enough co-founders; the last 8 visible posts (neighbours, the president's and nominees' speeches, chamber peers, never one's own); memory.
forum.decision: forum_post (thinking): a post, a change of mind (an issue and a direction: a fixed 0.25-logit step along that issue's latent loading), and a party move: join, leave, or found (needs co-founders ≥ 5% of citizens; for a year after a party is founded its members can neither found nor be brought into a founding, OBS-052). After any move, parties under half that size dissolve (seated parties and the last party are kept), and their members move to the nearest platform.
forum.schema: ForumTurn: rationale, post, note_to_self, shift_issue, shift_direction, party_move, party_id

opinion.name: Opinion dynamics
opinion.inputs: Two latent factors per citizen, their anchor, graph neighbours within the confidence bound.
opinion.decision: Friedkin-Johnsen with bounded confidence: f' = (1 − s)·anchor + s·(f + step·pull) + drift; positions are recomputed as sigmoid(f·loadings + residual). Spreads forum stance shifts through the graph and pulls citizens back toward their anchors.

legislation.name: Legislation
legislation.when: A bill every 2 ticks; a suspended bill's second reading when due.
legislation.who: The agenda setter (the government under cohabitation, otherwise the president), the assembly, the chamber.
legislation.inputs: Platforms, the president's position, seats, members' chamber positions.
legislation.decision: Draft: the top 2 priority-weighted gaps, each moved ≤ 0.1 (or the president agent's own bill). Assembly: each seated party votes yes iff the bill brings policy closer to its platform; passes above half the seats. Under cohabitation the president can block a bill that moves policy away from them. First reading only: the chamber reviews, and a majority against suspends the bill for 2 ticks. Then enacted.

amendments.name: Amendments & the constitution
amendments.when: Proposed on the president's turn; voted on the next tick, first phase.
amendments.who: The president proposes; every chamber member votes, blind, in parallel.
